Abstract: In a small language model the vocabulary is the single largest part. In Gemma 3 270M the embedding table holds 168M of 268M parameters, and because quantisation methods leave the embedding in 16-bit, it is also most of the file once the rest of the mo
items.summary: A new approach suggests using a frozen 16 MB vocabulary for small language models, significantly reducing parameter size and potentially lowering costs. This matters because the vocabulary typically makes up the largest portion of parameters in these models, and optimizing it could lead to more efficient and affordable language processing systems.
items.summary_detailed: The research paper "Embeddings Are Overpriced? A Frozen 16 MB Vocabulary for Small and Ternary Language Models" challenges the conventional approach to vocabulary size in small language models by proposing a frozen 16 MB vocabulary, significantly reducing the embedding table's size in models like Gemma 3 (270M parameters), where it previously held 168M of 268M parameters. This reduction not only optimizes parameter usage but also decreases file size, potentially lowering computational costs and improving efficiency for smaller language models.
